passage: In the Nakamura laboratory, researchers measured dehydrogenase activity in a liver homogenate by following production of NADH, which absorbs light at 340 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 6,220 M⁻¹cm⁻¹, whereas NAD⁺ does not absorb appreciably at this wavelength. The homogenate was diluted 10-fold in assay buffer before use, and 1 mL reactions in a 1 cm cuvette contained saturating substrate and NAD⁺ at 25 °C. Absorbance at 340 nm was recorded every minute. A blank containing all components except substrate was run in parallel to correct for non-enzymatic changes. The initial linear region of the progress curve was used to calculate velocity. The researchers wished to report the activity of the undiluted homogenate and to compare it with a published value from a different laboratory. The spectrophotometer was zeroed against buffer, and all readings fell within the instrument's linear range. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What is the change in A340 of the sample between 0 and 2 minutes, according to Table 1?
questions.trap: Reporting the raw 2-minute reading (0.299, option A) without subtracting the 0.05 starting absorbance.

questions.stem: Why is a blank lacking substrate included?

options.A: To detect absorbance changes that occur without the enzyme-catalyzed reaction
options.B: To ensure the enzyme is saturated
options.D: To increase the extinction coefficient of NADH

questions.explanation: The blank accounts for background drift (e.g., contaminating reductants, instrument drift) independent of the reaction under study.
questions.trap: Thinking the blank ensures enzyme saturation; it only reports background absorbance drift in the absence of the substrate-dependent reaction.

questions.stem: Using Beer–Lambert, what is the initial rate of NADH formation in the cuvette (µM/min), and what activity does the undiluted homogenate have (µM/min)?

options.A: 200 µM/min in the cuvette; 2000 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.B: 20 µM/min in the cuvette; 20 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.C: 0.02 µM/min in the cuvette; 0.2 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.D: 20 µM/min in the cuvette; 200 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate

questions.explanation: Rate = (ΔA/min)/(ε·l) = 0.1244/6220 = 20 µM/min in the cuvette. Multiply by the 10-fold dilution to get 200 µM/min for the undiluted homogenate.
questions.trap: Forgetting to multiply by the 10-fold dilution (option B gives 20 µM/min for both) or mis-scaling the values by a factor of 10 (option A).

questions.stem: Which statement about this assay is INCORRECT?

options.A: Substrate must be saturating for the rate to approximate Vmax
options.B: The initial linear portion of the curve gives the most reliable velocity
options.C: Both NAD⁺ and NADH absorb strongly at 340 nm, so the signal reflects total coenzyme
options.D: NADH absorbs at 340 nm while NAD⁺ does not

questions.explanation: Only the reduced coenzyme absorbs at 340 nm; that selective absorbance makes the assay possible.
questions.trap: Believing NAD+ also absorbs strongly at 340 nm so the signal reflects total coenzyme; only NADH absorbs, which is what makes the assay possible.

questions.stem: Which type of assay couples an enzyme of interest to NADH oxidation so that its activity can be monitored at 340 nm?

options.A: A gel assay using SDS-PAGE mobility
options.B: A coupled assay using lactate dehydrogenase to reduce pyruvate formed by pyruvate kinase
options.C: A radioactive assay using ³²P-labeled ATP
options.D: An immunoassay using antibodies against the enzyme

questions.explanation: Pyruvate kinase produces pyruvate; LDH then oxidizes NADH to NAD⁺, causing a decrease in A340 proportional to pyruvate kinase activity.
questions.trap: Choosing a gel, radioactive or antibody assay: none of these links the enzyme to NADH oxidation, so none gives a change in A340.
